content.text:
### Basic bind:value on input Source: https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/bind Binds the input's value to a state variable. The paragraph displays the current value. ```svelte

{message}

``` -------------------------------- ### Source: https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/bind A `bind:value` directive on an `` element binds the input’s `value` property: ```

{message}

``` -------------------------------- ### bind: Source: https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/bind Data ordinarily flows down, from parent to child. The `bind:` directive allows data to flow the other way, from child to parent. The general syntax is `bind:property={expression}`, where `expression` is an [_lvalue_](https://press.rebus.community/programmingfundamentals/chapter/lvalue-and-rvalue/) (i.e. a variable or an object property). When the expression is an identifier with the same name as the property, we can omit the expression — in other words these are equivalent: ``` ``` Svelte creates an event listener that updates the bound value. If an element already has a listener for the same event, that listener will be fired before the bound value is updated. Most bindings are _two-way_, meaning that changes to the value will affect the element and vice versa. A few bindings are _readonly_, meaning that changing their value will have no effect on the element. -------------------------------- ### Reactive declaration tags with $state and $derived Source: https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/declaration-tags Uses {let name = $state(...)} and {const greeting = $derived(...)} inside an {#if} block to create reactive local values. The greeting updates as the input changes. ```svelte

Hello {user.name}

{#if editing} {let name = $state(user.name)} {const greeting = $derived(`Hello ${name}`)}

{greeting}

{/if} ``` -------------------------------- ### Reactive declaration tags with $state and $derived (TypeScript) Source: https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/declaration-tags TypeScript version of the reactive declaration tags example, using lang="ts". ```svelte

Hello {user.name}

{#if editing} {let name = $state(user.name)} {const greeting = $derived(`Hello ${name}`)}

{greeting}

{/if} ```

content.text:
I added a search box above the list in `src/routes/+page.svelte`. It filters people by name as you type, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. If nothing matches, the list shows "No matches". `npm run check` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings. I didn't run the app in a browser, so the filtering itself is untested.

The Context7 docs returned Svelte 5 runes (`$state`, `$derived`). I didn't use them, because the project is on Svelte 4. I used `bind:value` with `$:` reactive statements instead.
